summary: A county forestry fire-watch tower built in 1937 in the San Gabriel wash near Temple, closed in 1947 and dismantled; no source found describes the site today.

facts.design: 8x8 observation cabin on an open steel tower, with a residence cabin and garage (tower height varies by source: 60, 70 or 75 ft)
facts.status_note: Dismantled soon after its 1947 closure; the property went back to the City of Monrovia.

events.note: County negotiated a lease for a lookout site four miles east of Temple, from Anna M. Spence of Monrovia at $5 a year
Tower and patrol station built by a CCC camp at Tuna Canyon; register gives 1937; the county's annual report says the work was done during the year
Dedicated June 2, 1937; William D. Reed was the first lookout operator
County fiscal 1947 annual report: abandoned because of rural development and public telephone reporting, after a detection study
Register: closed due to smog rendering the mountain view useless
Register: structure shortly thereafter dismantled; property returned to the City of Monrovia

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 75 feet; county annual reports say sixty feet; a January 1937 newspaper item says 70 feet. The brief's 21.3 m (70 ft) matches only the newspaper figure

The register says smog made the view useless; the county's fiscal 1947 annual report says changing conditions from rural development, public telephone reporting of fires, and a detection study led it to discontinue the tower

notes_for_editor: Only the register and Forest Lookouts were read, and a search for the site today found nothing, so the story says no source describes the site now. The height is unresolved (60, 70 or 75 ft), so the brief's height_m was left unchanged. The closure reason differs between sources. The 1936 and 1937 annual-report quotes are near-identical text; the 1937 year matches the register. Forest Lookouts quotes a 1935 article naming a Temple City location; the register puts the site on California Street, north of Arrow Highway.
